# Backend Engineer *at 3F Labs.*

3F is building the leverage layer for tokenized real-world assets: a Morpho-based vault protocol for leveraged exposure to tokenized CLOs, private credit, and fixed income through a single transaction.

We raised $4M from Maven 11, F-Prime, GSR, and Gate Ventures, and we are live on Ethereum mainnet with real capital. The team is six people.

Apply now

Level
:   Mid to senior

Location
:   Remote

Timezone
:   UK/EU overlap important; most of the team works UK/EU hours.

01

## The Role

### Ownership

Backend systems that coordinate leveraged positions across on-chain and off-chain settlement, with security as a default. The orchestration layer is where you would spend most of your time: coordinating bridge financing, Morpho collateral, stablecoin borrowing, transaction submission, and portfolio state under adversarial conditions.

* Design and build APIs for position management, auction mechanics, and portfolio tracking.
* Develop orchestration services for multi-step settlement workflows across bridge financing, Morpho collateral, and stablecoin borrowing.
* Integrate with on-chain protocols such as Morpho, Centrifuge, and Pareto/Idle: read state, submit transactions, and handle epoch-based settlement cycles.
* Extend and maintain cloud infrastructure on GCP/GKE using Terraform.
* Contribute to reliability and security: alerting, observability, database hardening, least-privilege access controls, and CI/CD pipelines.
* Own the security posture around audit logging, secret management, API boundaries, transaction-signing validation, and smart contract interaction safeguards.
* Review code with an adversarial lens, coordinate with auditors, and help triage bug bounty submissions as the protocol's attack surface grows.

02

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Core services | Rust (auction engine, orchestrator) |
| API layer | TypeScript / Node.js |
| Smart contracts | Solidity (Morpho integrations, facilitators) |
| Database | PostgreSQL (Cloud SQL) |
| Infrastructure | GCP, GKE, Terraform |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions, GKE |

03

## What We're Looking For

### How to read this role

You do not need every part of the stack on day one. The core signal is backend judgment: owning production systems, reasoning carefully about financial state, and learning unfamiliar protocols without hand-waving. DeFi helps, but strong engineers from fintech, infra, trading, payments, or security-heavy systems should feel welcome.

### Core signals

* Backend systems in production: APIs, data models, migrations, deploys, and operational tradeoffs.
* Strong Rust or TypeScript. Strength in one and willingness to learn the other is enough.
* Careful reasoning about financial state, permissions, signing flows, consistency, and failure modes.
* Production ownership mindset: tests, observability, clear rollback paths, and pragmatic release discipline.

### Helpful background

* Fintech, trading, payments, DeFi, crypto, or security-heavy infrastructure.
* Kubernetes, Terraform, GCP/GKE, or similar production platform work.
* Morpho, Aave, or other lending protocol exposure.
* Threat modeling, audit workflows, penetration testing, or bug bounty triage.

04

## Working at 3F

### How we work

* Small team, high autonomy. Everyone ships to production, without layers of approval.
* Weekly dev syncs, with async-first communication otherwise.
* You will work across the full backend surface: API endpoints, settlement orchestration, transaction flows, infrastructure provisioning, observability, and incident response.
* Specialization happens naturally, not by assignment.

### Production ownership

Because the team is small and the system handles real capital, this role includes production ownership and incident response. The goal is to make systems boring through observability, runbooks, testing, least-privilege access, and careful release process.

Apply

## Build the future *of onchain credit.*

Send a CV or relevant profile and a brief note on your background and interest in the role.

## Join AALTO in Farnborough as Senior Systems Engineer, integrating mission-critical onboard and ground software that enables Zephyr’s autonomous missions and unlocks Stratospace.

AALTO, a global leader in Stratospace. Based in Farnborough, AALTO is an Airbus subsidiary that manufactures, operates, and delivers services with its solar-powered, stratospheric platform: Zephyr.

Zephyr’s persistence enables continuous flight for months at a time. Its current flight-time record of over 67 days in the stratosphere. From above 60,000+ft, or 20km above ground, AALTO can deliver several applications including direct-to-device connectivity and high-resolution Earth observation.

AALTO operates in a new operational layer between most of air traffic and low-Earth orbit, Stratospace. This is where high-altitude platforms led by Zephyr deliver services to commercial and government partners. We can help monitor environments, observe borders, track natural disasters and connect unconnected communities.

Join us as we create a new domain of aerospace: Stratospace. You’ll be part of a highly-skilled, innovative and passionate group of people – Team AALTO. Together, we can Unlock Stratospace.

We are seeking a **Senior Systems Engineer** to join the team leading the development of the Zephyr High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS). In this role, you will play a key part in designing, developing, and integrating software systems—focusing on ground control and onboard software to enable seamless communication, control, and mission execution. You’ll work closely with cross-functional teams to deliver robust, scalable, and compliant software solutions that meet high standards for performance, safety, and regulatory compliance

* Identify and mitigate software-related risks, including cybersecurity, data integrity, and operational reliability.
* Act as a liaison between software teams and systems engineering, ensuring cohesive integration across avionics, payload, and ground systems.
* Maintain comprehensive documentation of software designs, test results, and integration procedures.

* Proven experience in software systems engineering, preferably in aerospace or UAV domains.
* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.
* Hands-on experience with onboard software development and ground control systems.
* Proficiency in network protocols (TCP, UDP), datalink technologies, and real-time systems.

* Experience with Systems Engineering tools (e.g., JAMA, IBM DOORS) and MBSE methodologies (desirable).

# Senior Product Manager - Account-to-Account Payments

## Sometimes the chance comes up to be part of something really special, at Acquired you’ll be collaborating with teams and people who challenge you, support you, and inspire you to be extraordinary.

**We’re Acquired**

At Acquired, we're on a mission to revolutionise recurring payments, and we're growing fast. We're building smart, customer-centric solutions by tackling complex problems with data, ingenuity, and a commitment to a **scalable, robust core platform**.

We are looking for an experienced, commercially minded, and deeply analytical Senior Product Manager to own our account-to-account payments portfolio, spanning collections and e-money. You will take Open Banking payments and Variable Recurring Payments from pilot to a repeatable product, own our Direct Debit capability, and shape the product implications of our e-money permissions.

---

**Your Mission**

As Senior Product Manager - Account-to-Account Payments, you'll own the strategy, roadmap, and execution across two areas: collections, covering Direct Debit and Open Banking payments including Variable Recurring Payments (UKPI and sweeping), and e-money.

Within that, the components sit at very different stages. Direct Debit is established and needs to perform. VRPs are at pilot, in a market that does not yet exist at scale. E-money is as much a regulatory build as a product one. Deciding what comes first, and defending that decision, is the core of the role.

Your core focus will be problem-based solving: combining deep data exploration with structured thinking to identify where merchants are underserved, set hypotheses, validate them with real merchants, and drive solutions forward to be built. Where a payment method is new to the market, the job is to hold two things together: validating demand before we commit to build, and making a deliberate strategic bet where the evidence will never be complete. We expect you to be clear about which of the two you are doing, and why.

This role requires you to act as a strategic problem-solver and hands-on validator, operating in a genuinely regulated environment: Bacs scheme rules, Open Banking standards, and the safeguarding obligations that come with holding customer funds.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, who owns product and engineering, you will drive commercial outcomes, increase revenue, and support business growth through structured product excellence.

---

###### **What You'll Be Doing**

**Strategy & Ownership**

* **Define and Own Strategy:** Define and own the roadmap and product strategy across collections and e-money, ensuring alignment with Acquired's strategic priorities, framing challenges as clear, solvable product problems, and making explicit calls about sequencing between them.
* **Anticipate & Adapt:** Anticipate market, scheme, and regulatory change, from the commercial VRP rollout to the direction of PSD3 and wider changes in UK payments regulation.

**Collections: Open Banking & VRPs**

* **Take VRPs to Market:** Own the path from pilot to repeatable product: which merchant segments first, what has to be proven before we scale, and what would stop a merchant moving a recurring collection off Direct Debit.
* **Validate Before Build:** Prove merchant demand and willingness to pay for capability the market has not adopted yet, using real conversations alongside data rather than internal assumption, and say so plainly when the evidence is not there.
* **Realise Value Incrementally:** Find the smallest slice that puts something live and useful in front of merchants, so that a long build returns value along the way rather than only at the end.
* **Own Journey Performance:** Treat completion rate through the bank authorisation journey as a product problem, working with the coverage, availability and app-to-app behaviour of individual banks that we do not control.
* **Measure Success:** Own the A2A metrics for success, such as payment completion rate, consent activation and reuse, and pilot to live conversion, using these as validation checkpoints.

**Collections: Direct Debit**

* **Direct Debit**: Own collection performance end to end, from mandate setup through to reducing failed payments and revenue leakage.
* **Investigate & Validate:** Proactively dive into payment performance data, not just to report metrics, but to uncover hidden problems (e.g. return reason clusters, per-bank failure patterns, specific merchant collection behaviours) and design experiments to solve them.
* **Recovery and Retries:** Own how failed collections are recovered, from retry timing and dunning to the merchant-facing tooling that reduces involuntary churn

**E-money**

* **Shape the Proposition:** Define what our e-money permissions unlock commercially, from holding merchant funds through to the products that become possible once we do, and make the call on what we build first.
* **Build the Foundations:** Own the product side of account structure, reconciliation and safeguarding, working closely with finance, compliance and engineering on a build that is as much regulatory as it is product.
* **Connect it to Collections:** Identify where e-money strengthens the wider A2A proposition, such as settlement timing and funds flow.

**Regulated Delivery & Partners**

* **Scheme and Regulatory Delivery:** Own the product side of Bacs scheme rules and the Direct Debit Guarantee, and Open Banking standards.
* **Partner Engagement**: Work with sponsor banks, indirect access providers, Open Banking providers and Pay.UK to expand and enhance our A2A capability and identify product partnerships.

* **Comfortable Creating a Market:** Able to work on a product where demand is not yet proven, and to say honestly when it is not there.
* **Hands-on:** Willing to conduct deep-dive analysis and personally drive the solution discovery process.

Our momentum comes from a simple idea: help teams work smarter, not harder. Aircall’s AI Voice Agent automates routine calls, AI Assist streamlines post-call work, and AI Assist Pro delivers real-time guidance so people can do their best work. Aircall is headquartered in Paris, our European HQ, with a strong North American presence anchored in Seattle, our North American HQ, and teams across Madrid, London, Berlin, San Francisco, New York City, Sydney, and Mexico City. We’ve built a product customers love and a business that’s scaling quickly, backed by world-class investors and driven by rapid AI innovation across multiple product lines.

At Aircall, you’ll join a company in motion. We’re ambitious, product-driven, and execution-focused, with visible impact, fast decisions, and real growth.

**How we work at Aircall**: We’re customer-obsessed, data-driven, and focused on delivering meaningful outcomes. We value ownership, continuous learning, and thoughtful speed. If you thrive in a collaborative, fast-moving environment where trust and impact matter, you’ll feel at home here.

**About the Team**

Aircall’s Forward Deployed Engineering team connects our innovative AI Agents technology to real-world SMB workflows. We turn possibility into production — delivering automation that improves customer experience, boosts productivity, and unlocks new business value. Working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales, Solutions, and Customer Success, the team ensures every deployment delivers measurable impact. This is a dynamic, hands-on role at the intersection of **technical consulting**, **project leadership**, and **AI adoption strategy**. You don’t need to be a full-time software engineer, but you should be fluent in APIs, very confident managing technical projects, and eager to continuously learn, build, and scale new models that empower both customers and teammates.

**About the Role**

As a Forward-Deployed Engineer, you’ll own the **end-to-end delivery** of technically sound, low-code AI solutions for Aircall customers. You’ll design, implement, and operationalize workflows that connect the AI Agent with CRMs, help desks, and communication tools. You’ll also play a key role in driving **team upskilling**, **building reusable frameworks**, and **leading cross-functional initiatives** that improve how Aircall deploys AI at scale. This is a hands-on role where you’ll translate customer challenges into scalable technical solutions, working directly with Product and Engineering to refine Aircall’s platform and accelerate adoption.

Please note, this is not a software engineering role. This is a hybrid, revenue driving role across Solutions Engineering, Software Engineering, Consulting, Professional Services, and Product Ownership

### What you'll do:

* **Lead customer discovery and design sessions** to map business processes, identify automation opportunities, and define solution architecture.
* **Design, build, and deploy integrations** using low/no-code platforms (Zapier, Make, n8n, Workato) and CRM automation tools (HubSpot Workflows, Salesforce Flow) with API connectors.
* **Collaborate with Engineering** to validate technical feasibility, resolve blockers, and share field learnings that inform product improvements.
* **Configure and optimize the AI Agent** — defining intents, prompts, actions, guardrails, and performance metrics.
* **Manage complex, cross-functional deployments** — defining timelines, aligning stakeholders, ensuring accountability, and delivering on time and within scope.
* **Create scalable models and reusable frameworks** (templates, playbooks, reference architectures) that make future projects faster and more consistent.
* **Champion continuous learning and enablement** — train peers, run internal workshops, and document best practices to raise the technical bar across the team.
* **Run global, targeted outbound campaigns** within the existing customer base to generate pipeline and accelerate adoption, working closely with the customer marketing team.
* **Collaborate with GTM leadership** to embed routines and cadences that drive accountability for new product pipeline, forecast accuracy, and performance tracking.
* **Own regional top-line targets** for assigned products (e.g., AI Voice Agent MRR generated per area) by collaborating with AEs and AMs who hold add-on quotas.
* **Act as an internal product owner** within the GTM function—defining product-specific MRR strategies, coordinating cross-functional support, and ensuring Aircall delivers the leading AI-enabled communication platform.
* **Collaborate with Product and PMM** to shape the AI Voice Agent roadmap based on customer needs, integration insights, and field learnings.
* **Drive internal and external product education**, including enablement for System Integrators (SIs) and channel partners.
* **Maintain deep awareness of AI and CX industry trends**, ensuring Aircall’s positioning remains competitive and insights continuously feed back into product and GTM strategies.

### What you'll bring:

* **0-6+ years of experience** in technical consulting, solutions engineering, or integration-focused project management.
* Strong command of **APIs, webhooks, and data structures (JSON, REST, GraphQL)** — able to design and troubleshoot integrations confidently. Even better if you have experience with MCP Servers.
* Hands-on experience with **low-code orchestration tools** (Zapier, Make, n8n, Workato) and **CRM automation** (HubSpot, Salesforce).
* Practical understanding of **AI workflow configuration**, including prompt engineering, evaluation, and monitoring.
* Proven ability to **lead cross-functional projects**, working with Engineering, Product, and Customer Success to deliver scalable outcomes.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, translating between technical and business audiences.
* A growth mindset — constantly learning new tools, frameworks, and ways to improve the customer experience and team capability.
* **Nice-to-haves:**
  + Experience in telephony, voice, or contact center systems (SIP/WebRTC, call routing, containment, AHT).
  + Familiarity with BI and analytics tools (Looker, BigQuery, Snowflake).
  + Exposure to scripting (JavaScript/Python) for light customization and debugging.

### What Success Looks Like:

* Consistent delivery of **high-quality, scalable AI Agent deployments** with clear business outcomes.
* Shortened **time-to-first-value** and increased automation adoption across SMB customers.
* Reusable frameworks, models, and templates actively used by peers and partners.
* Strong collaboration with Engineering and Product to enhance platform capabilities.
* Demonstrated leadership in **team enablement and upskilling**, with measurable impact on technical excellence.
* Sustained improvements in customer metrics (containment, AHT, CSAT) and revenue impact (ARR, NRR) driven by your solutions

**Why This Role is Unique**

This is a role for builders, connectors, and enablers. You’ll be at the intersection of AI innovation, customer experience, and scalable delivery — combining technical curiosity with a consulting mindset. Every project you lead not only delivers value for customers but also strengthens Aircall’s internal capability to deploy AI faster and smarter.

If you’re motivated by making cutting-edge technology accessible and impactful — while continuously learning and helping others do the same — this is the perfect next step in your career.

# Regional Manager EMEA, Data Center Capacity Delivery

London, UK

## **About Anthropic**

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

## **About the role**

Training and serving frontier AI models requires data center capacity at a scale and pace that conventional delivery models were not built for. Anthropic's Data Center Capacity Delivery team embeds with developers, general contractors, and third-party partners to take leased and partnered sites from deal close through floor access and operational handover as fast as they can safely be built.

As a Regional Manager, you'll own delivery across a regional portfolio of active and upcoming projects. You'll build and lead the team of Senior Delivery Managers and third-party partners who sit on those sites, set the standards they execute to, and step in yourself where a project needs it. You are the executive-level interface to our developer partners in the region and the intake point for projects handed over from our transaction team.

This is a highly cross-functional role: you'll work daily with our transaction, design engineering, facility operations and commissioning, deployment, and safety teams, and with developers, GCs, and owner's-representative firms on the ground.

## **MOC (Mission + Outcomes + Competencies)**

### **Mission**

Deliver the region’s data center projects to floor access as fast as they can safely be built.

### **Outcomes**

* Every active project in the region delivered against early-floor-access and floor-access milestones.
* Senior Delivery Manager team hired and led; owner’s-rep partners contracted and managed.
* Delivery standards (schedule, quality, change control, reporting) enforced across the portfolio.
* Executive reporting on progress vs plan and regional capacity projections in place.

### **Competencies**

* Senior owner- or GC-side mission-critical delivery leadership.
* Builds and leads multi-project teams.
* Executive-level developer and GC relationship management.
* Leads on site through presence; owns outcomes where no process exists.

## **Responsibilities**

* Lead. This is a role where leadership trumps management and process. You are expected to be on the region's sites enough to shape the culture, approach, and aggressiveness that define the extended teams there — across the portfolio, not one project — and to impact outcomes in a favorable manner.
* Be a force multiplier. Hire, develop, empower, and lead the Senior Delivery Managers on those sites, and raise the skillset developers, contractors, owner's-rep partners, and key trades bring to every project in the region; plan resourcing and headcount as the portfolio grows.
* Own portfolio execution for the region — schedule, quality, and safety outcomes on every active project, measured against early-floor-access and floor-access milestones. You are empowered and have autonomy to own this regions record of performance.
* Drive ownership and influence both inside and outside contractual structures: select, scope, contract, and manage owner's-rep and project-management partners; where contracts, incentives, or culture get in the way of speed, change them, and replace partners when performance or culture slips
* Set and enforce delivery standards across projects — integrated schedule, quality requirements, change control, reporting, and tools — and validate that they are met
* Identify blockers early and clear them across developer, GC, and trade layers; step in on site where a project needs it

## **You may be a good fit if you**

* Have [10+] years delivering data center or other mission-critical construction, including several as the owner's or GC's senior leader on a project campus
* Have led a multi-project portfolio and built the team that delivered it
* Know the end-to-end development process — entitlements and permitting, design, long-lead equipment, construction, commissioning, and handover — well enough to direct partners rather than take their word for it
* Have managed developer, GC, and third-party relationships at the executive level and can move them from arm's-length contract administration to shared urgency
* Lead through presence: you expect to be on site most of the time and to set the pace and culture of extended teams you don't directly employ
* Communicate clearly with technical and non-specialist stakeholders and hold a position when challenged
* Are comfortable with ambiguity and with owning outcomes where no process exists yet

## **Strong candidates may also have**

* Hyperscale data center delivery experience on the owner, developer, or GC side
* Experience with the UK and continental European market — its contractors, permitting regimes, and contractual norms
* Familiarity with lease, construction, and development contract structures and how to align their incentives around speed

Annual Salary:

£1 - £1 GBP

## **Logistics**

**Minimum education:** Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

**Required field of study:**A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

**Minimum years of experience:** Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

**Location-based hybrid policy:** Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

**Visa sponsorship:** We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

## **How we're different**

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

## **Come work with us!**

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. Imagine what you could do here! At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming
extraordinary products, services, and experiences very quickly — and that is as
true of the tools we build for engineers inside Apple as it is of the products
the world sees. Our team builds platforms that engineering teams across Apple
Services Engineering depend on. When we get it right, complicated work becomes
simpler and faster, and the platform itself gets out of the way. With the advent
of artificial intelligence, the way software gets built has changed, and this
role is written for this new era of AI-assisted engineering. We are looking for
an engineer who is, at heart, a builder who works fluently with agentic AI
coding assistants. Someone who is equally at home crafting a refined React user
interface and designing the distributed Java services and data flows behind it.
AI tools have made producing code far faster; they have not made it any more
trustworthy. Driving generated code to the point where it can be trusted to meet
the requirements is the part of the job we weigh most heavily. If you care about
elegant systems as much as elegant code, and you have already reorganized your
own software development workflows around AI tools, we would like to hear from
you.


DESCRIPTION


You will design, build, and evolve software products, services, and tools in the
Solutions Platforms and Architecture team. The work spans the full stack: the
user interfaces engineers use, the services and API contracts behind them, and
the pipelines that carry all of it into production. You will own features from
problem definition and technical design through implementation, deployment,
adoption, and continuous improvement. We care deeply about the experience of the
people who use what we build. We think in systems: how components fit together,
where the right abstractions belong, and how today's decisions shape tomorrow's
roadmap. You will bring that same user-first instinct to interfaces and APIs
that are a delight to use and to integrate with. The systems underneath are
large-scale and distributed, and one of the real challenges of this role lives
there. Services fail partially, writes arrive out of order, and state is often
eventually consistent — and every one of those facts surfaces at the edge,
whether that edge is a person watching a browser or another system calling our
API. You will handle that complexity end to end: designing services that stay
correct under concurrency, and deciding what a caller sees in the meantime — how
the interface behaves when an optimistic update has to be reconciled or rolled
back, and what guarantees the API contract provides to a client that retries.
Working with AI runs through all of that, and using agentic AI well is a
fundamental expectation of this role. We expect you to use the latest frontier
models and AI best practices so that you can leverage AI to amplify the entire
software development lifecycle, including interactive planning, architecture,
design, product requirements, product user stories, test plans, TDD code
generation, iterative code review and refinement, pull request reviews,
diagnostics, and performance analysis. You will seek out review of your own work
and give candid feedback on your colleagues' work — including when the honest
answer is that something is not yet good enough. You will discuss implementation
proposals with the team, argue for the approach you believe in, and commit fully
to the decision that gets made. Testing is a primary engineering activity here,
not a step at the end. You will design unit, integration, and end-to-end
coverage that gives the team genuine confidence to release, and build the CI/CD
pipelines and scripting that run it continuously. You will gather requirements
from stakeholders and turn them into a plan, including when the requirements
arrive incomplete. Naming what is still unknown and moving forward anyway is
part of the job, and you will correct course as things become clear rather than
wait for certainty. You will participate in production releases, coordinate
deployments, communicate with customers and stakeholders, support users of our
team's software, and act on reliability improvements when you spot the
opportunity. This work depends on close collaboration within our team and with
the teams we support, so the role asks for curiosity, communication, and
ownership alongside strong engineering judgment.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS


Experience in using agentic AI coding assistants, Claude Code or equivalent, as
a primary development tool: engineering the LLM context, structuring effective
prompts, building reusable agents and agent skills, planning through interactive
discussion with the model, and carrying a feature from intent through to
reviewed, tested, and deployed code. Strong software architecture and design
fundamentals: decomposing systems into services with clear boundaries, applying
design patterns deliberately, designing REST API contracts, and reasoning about
failure modes, data flow, and how a design will age. Proven experience designing
and building automated tests at every level (unit, integration, and end-to-end)
including end-to-end test suites reliable enough to gate a release, and the
judgment to say what a passing suite does and does not prove about meeting the
requirements. Front-end development with TypeScript and JavaScript, building
user interfaces in React and working with the Node.js tooling around them.
Back-end service development in Java, implementing and consuming REST APIs.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


Fluency in reading, reviewing, and critically evaluating code you did not write,
including code a model generated. Experience building on large-scale distributed
systems, and handling the asynchronous complexity they create end to end:
concurrency and race conditions in services, eventual consistency across
regional and system boundaries, optimistic updates in the interface, and
idempotent, retry-safe API contracts. Hands-on experience building and
maintaining CI/CD pipelines, with the bash scripting that holds them together —
code you generate, review, and qualify comfortably. Experience defining testing
or CI/CD standards for a team, rather than only working within standards someone
else set. Event-driven architecture using messaging queues or platforms.
Containerized deployment with Docker and Kubernetes. Observability practice:
instrumenting services and using logs, metrics, and traces to understand real
production behavior. Comfortable working in a macOS or Linux terminal as a
primary environment.

* Build trusted relationships across senior leadership, operational, business and technology teams. Bring constructive challenge, use evidence to test assumptions, and be prepared to push back respectfully when proposals add unnecessary complexity, weaken the intended outcome or do not represent the best use of organisational capacity.

## About ELR

E-Invoicing and Live Reporting (ELR) is Avalara's product line for government-mandated electronic invoicing and real-time tax reporting. As more countries pass legislation requiring digital invoice exchange and live reporting to tax authorities, companies operating in those jurisdictions must comply. Avalara ELR gives businesses a single API and platform to meet these requirements across countries, replacing the fragmented, country-by-country local solutions most companies would otherwise need to stitch together.

## Overview

Avalara is seeking a Director of Finance & Strategy to serve as the embedded finance partner — effectively a mini-CFO — to the ELR General Manager. This role will spend approximately 75% of its time driving the ELR P&L, growth strategy, and operating rhythm alongside the ELR GM, and approximately 25% of its time providing FP&A partnership to Avalara's non-ELR Sales leaders across EMEA. The role reports solid-line to the SVP, Finance & Strategy and dotted-line to the ELR GM, ensuring both close day-to-day partnership with the business and full integration into Avalara's broader finance organization, standards, and reporting cadence.

This is a high-visibility, high-ownership role for a finance leader who wants true operating partnership with a strategically important, fast-growing product line, while also building broader cross-functional exposure through EMEA GTM finance support. The ideal candidate combines strong financial modeling and analytical rigor with the business judgment and communication skills to operate as a genuine co-pilot to the business, not just a reporting function.

  
What Your Responsibilities Will Be  
  

### ELR Finance Partnership (~75%)

* Serve as the primary finance partner to the ELR General Manager, functioning as a mini-CFO for the product line — embedded in strategy, operating reviews, and day-to-day decision-making.
* Own ELR's financial plan, forecast, and long-range model, connecting bookings, ARR growth, pricing, and cost structure to overall product line performance.

# Senior SOC Analyst / Manager

**Full Time,
Worldwide / Hybrid / Remote (HQ - Reading, England)**

Employees are expected to split their time among office locations, client sites, and remote work.

---

Baleen Labs is a small, highly capable technology consultancy serving clients in high-stakes operational environments. Over nearly five years, we have modernised legacy technology stacks, developed data strategies that unlock business value, and led transformation and optimisation initiatives.

In response to client demand, we are establishing an Information Security & Operations team. This team addresses inconsistencies across security posture, tenancy management, and endpoint control. We are building a small group of specialists distributed across multiple time zones to deliver follow-the-sun coverage for our clients.

### Mission

The SOC Manager / Senior Security Analyst will lead threat detection, incident response, and forensic investigation capabilities that deliver rapid visibility and containment without compromising operational continuity.

Our initial engagement involves a key client in the business aviation sector. Success requires proving that rigorous security monitoring can coexist with mission-critical flight operations, ensuring continuous surveillance for active threats while maintaining high alert precision and minimising disruptions to crew effectiveness.

### Why This Work Matters

In high-stakes environments, security failures carry consequences beyond data breaches. For our aviation client, delayed threat detection directly affects operational safety and crew effectiveness. Undetected compromise creates invisible attack surfaces that compromise mission assurance.

### What Good Looks Like

Our approach rejects process for its own sake. We implement the right level of monitoring for the specific risk profile, balancing protection with operational continuity. This pragmatism ensures security enables rather than hinders the work our clients depend on.

Good performance in this role means demonstrating forensic rigour, investigative depth, and incident command capability from day one. You understand that enterprise frameworks often contain redundant layers unsuitable for lean, agile in-house teams. You can distinguish between effective necessity and administrative overhead. You work in “best option right now” day-to-day, while keeping in mind “absolute best practice” so that the former necessarily leads towards the latter at an appropriate pace.

You help build team accountability so team members operate without single points of failure, and each person has enough breadth to support adjacent domains when needed. Knowledge is shared openly rather than siloed. Handovers are precise and documented. Trust is built across distances through clear communication and consistent delivery.

Success is measured by resilient detection systems that withstand adversarial evasion, incident response that operates under constraint, and investigations that remain thorough in air-gapped or degraded connectivity conditions. Success also includes growing team capability over time, not just maintaining current performance levels.

### Who We Are Looking For

These are not entry-level or “follow-the-script” roles. Mission-driven individuals thrive here, especially those who can think critically, operate with minimal supervision, and refuse to rely on AI to substitute for their own analysis.

We’re looking for practitioners who understand that security is *a discipline of judgement, not automation*. If you expect out-of-the-box solutions to work without custom configuration, this position will frustrate you. If you view frameworks as starting points rather than prescriptions, you will thrive here.

### The Role

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Oversee AI-supported SOC operations, acting as final arbiter for escalated incidents
* Execute follow-the-sun operations with continuous investigation threads across shifts and flawless handover documentation
* Integrate threat intelligence feeds and immediately update detection rules and playbooks for emerging TTPs including ransomware and phishing campaigns
* Coordinate penetration testing and lead breach monitoring activities
* Provide Tier 2/3 support during the aviation proof of concept rollout
* Connect dots between unrelated events that indicate active adversary presence
* Tune detection logic to reduce noise while preserving signal quality
* Lead incident command during security events and ensure proper escalation pathways
* Mentor Tier 1/2 analysts through structured feedback sessions and case reviews
* Develop competency pathways that enable analysts to progress from triage to independent investigation
* Receive escalated investigations from Tier 1/2 analysts with complete chain of custody and context

**Likely** **Background:**

* Strong grounding in digital forensics and incident investigation
* Experience solving problems in unreliable connectivity environments
* Working knowledge of SIEM platforms and their role in threat detection
* Evidence of adapting frameworks rather than applying them rigidly
* Experience in blue team operations with demonstrated incident command experience
* Experience building and leading small teams or shifts

### Phenotype

**Systems Thinking:** You understand how people, processes, technology and risk interact. You can assess whether a process is achieving its intended outcome, remove unnecessary complexity and adapt enterprise practices for lean, agile teams.

**Pragmatic Risk Management:** You make proportionate, defensible decisions based on impact, likelihood and available evidence. You distinguish meaningful risk reduction from process theatre and understand that excessive control can create operational fragility.

**Independent Judgement:** You can lead investigations and make decisions in ambiguous or time-sensitive situations. You know when to act, when to seek input and when an issue requires escalation beyond the SOC.

**Operational Improvement:** You look beyond individual alerts to identify recurring weaknesses in detection, response, tooling, configuration and process. You turn operational experience into measurable improvements rather than accepting repeated problems as inevitable.

**Technical Depth:** You understand how systems behave beneath their abstraction layers, including the relationships between endpoints, networks, identity, cloud services, applications and logging platforms. You are comfortable investigating custom environments where out-of-the-box solutions are insufficient.

**Detection and Investigation Mindset:** You think in terms of attacker behaviour, evidence, dependencies and likely impact. You can distinguish signal from noise, test competing hypotheses and improve detections based on lessons from real investigations.

**Emerging Threat and Risk Awareness:** You maintain a current understanding of emerging threats, attack techniques, vulnerabilities and changes in the risk environment. You assess their relevance to the organisation, translate meaningful developments into practical changes to monitoring and response, and act before new risks become incidents.

**Team Continuity:** You maintain sufficient breadth across adjacent technical domains to provide effective cover when specialists are unavailable. You can work with unfamiliar technologies, establish a practical understanding quickly and help others do the same.

**Leadership Through Practice:** You raise standards through the quality of your decisions, documentation, investigations and communication. You coach less experienced analysts, share context generously and help the team become less dependent on individual expertise.

**Global Collaboration:** You work effectively in a distributed team. You communicate clearly across time zones, maintain precise records, conduct reliable handovers and build trust through consistent follow-through.

**Discretion:** To the outside world, including friends and family in casual settings, you "work in IT". You do not discuss who the organisation serves, what it secures or the specifics of its work. Your professional reputation is protected by disciplined confidentiality.

### Outcomes

Within the first thirty days:

* Define and document a streamlined operating model, including follow-the-sun workflow and handover protocols
* Complete a baseline assessment of current monitoring coverage against industry standards
* Establish internal knowledge repositories and initial detection rule configurations
* Onboard and assess the Tier 1/2 analyst to identify competency gaps and development priorities

Within sixty days:

* Launch the aviation sector proof of concept, executing log source integration, detection engineering, and playbook deployment for flight operations
* Ensure critical security telemetry remains visible in offline or low-connectivity environments
* Eliminate blind spots by consolidating alert streams into secure, managed dashboards
* Validate that security controls do not impede operational safety
* Achieve a fully functional, secure, and resilient monitoring environment

Beyond ninety days:

* Refine detection logic based on aviation proof of concept feedback
* Begin expanding monitoring coverage for broader business units
* Conduct workshops with client IT leads to define incident escalation boundaries
* Roll out threat hunting programmes and tabletop exercises to additional clients
* Re-evaluate all deployed controls against emerging adversary TTPs
* Document competency pathways and progression milestones for junior analysts

### Position: Senior CPU Design Engineer

ARM Holdings is seeking an experienced Senior CPU Design Engineer to join our CPU Group in Cambridge, UK. * Design and implement microarchitectural blocks for ARM Cortex‐A and/or Neoverse V series processors using Verilog/SystemVerilog.

* Experience with low‐power design techniques (power gating, clock gating, DVFS).

* Familiarity with Armv8‐A or Armv9 architecture.

## How you can make your mark

Make your mark as **Offshore Project Engineer** for Boskalis Subsea Services located offshore and onshore when required.  You will be focal point for the mobilisation and demobilisations, you will also work in conjunction with the onshore Remote Operations Centre (ROC) during offshore execution phase.  You have a combined role;

* Focal point for mobilisations and de-mobilisations.
* Fulfil project engineer duties.
* Provide onshore support to projects/initiatives if/as required

**Your responsibilities as Offshore Project Engineer:**

The main responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

* Provide leadership during mobilisations and demobilisations to ensure that the activities are delivered safely and efficiently in accordance with approved deck plans or as amended where necessary through the Management of Change process.
* Ensure deck plans, lift plans, and mobilisation plans are received and reviewed prior to Mobilisation.
* Verify that all project equipment is delivered with suitable documentation / certification and tested prior to sailing.
* The Offshore Project Engineer will perform the role of Project Engineer during the offshore phase of the project.
* Support the onshore Remote Operations Centre (ROC) and act as lead engineers offshore if ROC connectivity fails.
* Monitor performance of offshore subcontractors against project deliverables, ensuring compliance with standards and schedules.
* Oversee the delivery of engineering tasks, installation sequences, and operational procedures as instructed by the ROC, providing real-time progress, technical observations, and operational constraints as required.
* Maintain onboard control of all project documentation, drawings, procedures, and ROC updates, ensuring latest revisions are used.

## We offer

You can make your mark as **Offshore Project Engineer** if you have:

* 3-4 years minimum Project/Field Engineering experience in Subsea Construction and/or IRM environments. DSV and CSV exposure desirable.
* Engineering qualification (HNC or above – Mechanical/Civil) or relevant knowledge obtained through practical experience in all aspects of the Offshore Project Engineer role
* Ability to deliver complex mobilisation and offshore operation activities.
* OPITO BOSIET/FOET with CA-EBS, MIST and OEUK Medical.

**What you can expect**

* A dynamic environment: A job that allows you to collaborate with a talented team of experts from different backgrounds and contribute to making a significant impact.

* Career development: We offer you plenty of opportunities to bring out the best in yourself for example through (online) courses at our Boskalis academy.
* Opportunities to connect with colleagues across the organization: Through networking and knowledge-sharing sessions, events, and employee communities.

**Extra information**

* Your team:  you will work closely with the Engineering, Project and Offshore teams and various departments throughout the business.
* Where you will work: you will be primarily based offshore on our DSVs and/or CSV with some  time spent in the Aberdeen office as required.
* Full/part- time job: The position of Offshore Project Engineer is based on a Guaranteed Day Contract.
* Next steps: Apply easily by completing the online application form. Interviews are held online or in the office. Once it’s clear we’re a good match, we’ll make you an offer – and look forward to welcoming you to the company.

## Job Description

**Overview**  
  

Certara accelerates the potential of bringing medicines to market and to patients using biosimulation software, technology, and services to transform traditional drug discovery and development. Our goal is to enable the life sciences industry’s use of data, modeling, and analytics to make better decisions across the various phases of discovery and drug development. Our software and scientists incorporate modern advances in scientific understanding, drug development experience, data analysis, and AI resulting in significant opportunities to decrease the cost and increase the probability of success for new drug approval and commercialization.

We have an opening for a highly motivated Research Scientist to work on research and development of mechanistic models for small and large molecules implemented within various Simcyp products using mathematical models and robust statistical data analysis techniques. The Scientist should have some familiarity with physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling and *in vitro-in vivo* extrapolation approaches.

Suitable candidates will have experience in applied mathematics, biostatistics and data analysis. Experience in the development of Bayesian inference methods and multilevel statistical models would be particularly appreciated. The successful candidate is expected to keep abreast of the latest scientific developments, disseminate research results, and actively engage with peers and clients within industry, academia and regulatory agencies. Experience working in drug discovery and development within the pharmaceutical industry is desirable.

 

The successful candidate will join an internationally recognised, multidisciplinary research team, providing opportunities for further development of knowledge and skills. The candidate will undertake novel research projects to expand further the capabilities of the Simcyp Simulators, which require a high level of attention to detail, good oral and written communication skills, and the ability to liaise effectively with the software developers. Further, the candidate is expected to provide on-going customer support and education related to the use of the Simulators and to act as tutor on the Company’s well-known educational workshops. The post does not include routine laboratory or clinical work.

  
**Responsibilities**  
  

Active involvement in research and development of PBPK/PD models implemented within the Simcyp Simulators including collating, reviewing and analysing healthy and disease populations as well as compound and clinical data.

* Preparing implementation documents and developing case studies under guidance or independently leading wish-list and/or strategic projects as needed.
* Contributing to consultancy projects when required.
* Applying your experience/expertise in assisting with development and enhancement of module for modelling and simulation of various organs and tissues.
* Flexibility to learn and work on projects in areas outside of your previous experience e.g., absorption modules when required.
* Training up to act as a tutor for Simcyp workshops when and if needed.
* Take on a substantial role in testing the Simulators before and after the release.
* Disseminating the outcome of research as poster/podium presentations and scientific publications.
* Communicating with clients and dealing with clients’ queries.
* Taking part in clients’ site visits and on-site education.
* Assisting with the research and development of externally funded projects e.g., grants.
* Maintaining an active interest and awareness of new research and technologies relevant to the field, expanding your field expertise, and disseminating these within the team

  
**Qualifications**  
  

* Master's or higher degree in Applied Mathematics, Statistics or related fields with several years of relevant practical experience.
* In-depth understanding and hands-on experience in modelling and simulation principles, statistical data analysis, parameter fitting and sensitivity analysis.
* Good working knowledge of common or specialised modelling and simulation tools, such as Matlab, R, Phoenix, Simcyp, etc.
* Familiarity with AI tools and their applications.
* Excellent record of communication skills, as evident by presentation at scientific meetings, and good interpersonal and organizational skills.

Desirable

* Experience in the development of Bayesian inference methods and multilevel statistical models
* Proven track record of publications in high impact factor journals.

# Customer Support Team Lead (Remote within the UK)

## At Chip, our mission is to make our customers wealthier. An app to build your long-term wealth across savings, investments and pensions.

We usually respond within three days

Chip is on a mission to make saving and investing effortless for everyone. With a product suite spanning savings, ISAs, and investment accounts, we're now launching our SIPP pension — and we're looking for the right person to help us get it right for customers from day one.

This role sits at the heart of one of Chip's most significant product launches. As we bring our SIPP pension to market, we're looking for a Team Lead who can help shape what great customer support looks like from day one, and grow with the proposition as it evolves. As Chip's proposition matures, our ambition is to move toward more personalised, regulated support for customers, and this individual is likely to play a leading role in shaping how CS delivers that. If you're motivated by helping build something, not just running it, this is the right opportunity.

You'll be part of a broader CS team, leading on Pensions while contributing to the wider range of customer queries and subjects across Chip's product suite. You'll report to the Customer Service Manager and work closely with colleagues across CS leadership to ensure consistency in standards, process, and direction.

**What you can expect to be doing:**

***Pensions SME***

* The go-to person within CS for all things pension and SIPP — building and maintaining internal knowledge, guidance, and processes as the product evolves
* Primary CS liaison with the Product team — translating customer insight into actionable feedback, flagging friction points, and contributing to the pension customer experience roadmap
* Keeping across regulatory developments relevant to SIPP and pension products and ensuring the team is always up to speed
* Playing an active role in how Chip develops more personalised, regulated support for customers over time

***Leading your team***

* Day-to-day line management of a broader CS team with a Pensions specialism — setting the standard, driving performance, and developing people
* 1-2-1s, probation reviews, personal OKRs, and performance management
* Experienced in having difficult conversations and comfortable holding people to account with fairness and consistency
* Creating an environment where people are motivated, supported, and clear on what good looks like

***Operational responsibilities***

* Representing Customer Support in the Pensions work stream — SLAs, KPIs, blockers, and solutions
* Rota management, leave, sickness cover, and OOH planning — always with a risk-based eye on customer impact
* Supporting the team with complex pension enquiries and acting as the escalation point when it matters
* Using data to understand performance, spot trends, and drive continuous improvement
* Ensuring full compliance with FCA regulatory requirements across every customer interaction

**What we’re looking for:**

***Essential***

* Experience managing customer support teams within an FCA-regulated financial services environment, pensions, investments, mortgages, financial advice, or similar
* A solid grasp of the compliance obligations that come with supporting customers on regulated products
* A natural subject matter expert, someone who builds knowledge, shares it well, and uses it to influence across teams
* A people-first leader with a genuine track record of developing and getting the best out of a team
* Operationally sharp, comfortable with data, SLAs, and the day-to-day reality of running a busy CS function
* Motivated by helping build and shape, not just maintain

***Desirable***

* Direct SIPP or pension product experience
* Experience in or adjacent to environments moving toward more personalised, regulated customer support

**What we’re really looking for:** ✍️

We’re looking for someone who’s genuinely excited about Chip and energised by the opportunity to help build the future of wealth, making saving, investing and pensions simpler and more accessible for everyone.

We work in a regulated space, so the bar is high. But we’ve built a team of smart, thoughtful people who care about doing great work and enjoy doing it together. Technical skills matter, obviously. But they’re not the only thing we hire for.

We want real people. People with interests, perspective and personality. The best teams are made up of individuals who bring different experiences into the room, not just polished CVs and good interview answers.

So alongside the technical side, we’ll be looking for empathy, self-awareness, sound judgement, resilience and a collaborative mindset. People who are good to work with, especially when things get hard.

⏰ **Working Hours** ⏰

* **Monday to Thursday:** 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM
* **Friday:** 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM (Start your weekend early!)

Enjoy a **structured yet balanced** workweek, with an early Friday finish to kickstart your weekend!

**PERKS** 🎁

* £35,000 - £40,000 per annum
* Discretionary Performance-Related Annual Bonus
* Workplace pension scheme - We invest in your future with a **workplace pension scheme**, contributing **5% on earnings up to £40,000**. Plan ahead with confidence while you grow your career! 🚀
* Private medical insurance (medical history disregarded)
* Employee Assistance Programme
* Cycle to work scheme
* Season ticket loan
* Free ChipX subscription for UK-based employees
* We are an equal-opportunity employer and value diversity
* Flexible working arrangements
* 28 days holiday plus bank holidays, plus the days between Christmas and New Year ✈️
* Annual training budget for courses, workshops, or conferences to help you advance your career.

* **Mission-Driven**: We focus on creating economic and social impact.

If you’re ready to earn, learn, serve, and be part of a vibrant global community, CloudFactory is your place!

**About the Role**

We are seeking a dedicated and motivated Data Capture Technician to operate reality capture equipment, such as 360-degree cameras and other surveying tools, in a variety of environments. The technician will be responsible for capturing comprehensive data of construction sites using different equipment and methodologies that align with algorithmic analysis.

We are looking for someone who is hardworking, responsible, and passionate about fieldwork, with the ability to effectively use technology to collect detailed site information. This is a part-time role, requiring one day of work per week.

**What You'll Do**

* Capture high-quality site data using **360° cameras and other data capture equipment** across active construction sites.
* Document site progress accurately by collecting visual data that supports project tracking and AI-powered construction solutions.
* Follow all site safety procedures and wear the required **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)** at all times to ensure your safety and the safety of those around you.
* Work closely with the Project Team Lead to meet project requirements and adapt to changing site conditions.
* Handle and maintain company equipment responsibly, ensuring all captured data meets quality standards.
* Follow detailed instructions and complete data capture tasks accurately and consistently.

## Requirements

**What We're Looking For**

* Availability to work **at least one full day per week** **(Friday)** during daytime hours.
* Comfortable working on **active construction sites** while following all safety requirements.
* Able to walk **up to 20,000+ steps per day** and perform light physical activities as part of the role.
* Willing to wear the required **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)** and work in various weather conditions.
* A positive attitude, reliability, and the ability to work well as part of a team.
* Flexible, adaptable, and able to solve problems in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to follow detailed instructions accurately and consistently.
* Comfortable using smartphones, tablets, or other technology to capture and record data.
* Previous fieldwork experience is an advantage.
* A background in **Construction, Surveying, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Site Inspections, Photography, or Reality Capture** is highly preferred.

**Important: Please read before applying.** This is not a standard videography or flexible freelance gig. We are looking for **reliable, punctual, and physically active** individuals to capture critical data on active construction sites.

**The logistics:**

* **Part-Time:** Each construction site requires 1–2 days of capture per week. This is not a full-time role unless you are willing and able to cover multiple sites within your region.

Hi I’m Colin, Director of Engineering, Europe. How do you feel about software engineers writing product specs, making product decisions, and not breaking down projects into individual tickets? If that sounds exciting (even if a bit scary), read on because I’m looking for an engineering manager to help us build a different type of engineering team and culture at Ashby.  
  
To start, why do we need to be different? Time and again, I have witnessed engineers knowing what needs to be done yet being unable to get things done because of “the process” or because “more data is needed.” Some of the most effective projects have been skunkworks projects, where engineers have taken total ownership of a problem and driven it to completion. I want to normalize that at Ashby.  
  
When we think about how these processes came about, we realize they carry a pessimistic mindset. They box people into smaller roles to minimize the chance of not meeting a certain standard. At Ashby. we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve and embraces the innovative engineers (and frankly, often stays out of their way).  
  
To accomplish this, our engineering leaders need to think deeply about individual performance, process, and culture - not running sprint planning or driving product and technical decisions. You’ll focus on building your team, their skills to thrive with the ownership they’re given, and an environment that empowers them to do their best work consistently, with little distraction. For junior EMs we try to stay within 6 direct reports. This enables them to spend time with our teams observing, correcting, praising, and, yes, coding. We like our managers to be hands-on while also making sure they’re not on the critical path.  
  
We’ve already gathered an experienced, talented, and collaborative team of 25+ engineers. You’ll help me manage the growing team of engineers in Europe.  
  
In addition to working with engineers you’ll also get to work on projects yourselves. Some examples of work our engineering leaders have done:  
  
•  
  
Provide feedback on product and technical specs to help engineers identify where to cut scope or improve quality. You don’t make the final decisions, but you’ll influence and coach ICs to reach the right ones.  
  
•  
  
Grow engineers to the point where they can take large, loosely defined projects, and deliver them with little intervention. They still ask for help when needed - the difference is that they’re driving.  
  
•  
  
Jump into our systems and code to debug a customer issue, ship a small bug fix, or improve our developer experience. Engineering leaders at Ashby are great engineers and enjoy keeping their skills up-to-date (while staying off the critical path).  
  
•  
  
Improve how we generate and simulate data in demo accounts. It’s a project off the critical path, but it helps you keep up-to-date on our codebase while immensely impacting the business, from Engineering to QA to Sales.  
  
Why be a manager?  
  
I had two experiences early in my career that set me on my path. I had a great manager who asked tonnes of questions about the decisions I was making and coached me without me realizing it. And I had a terrible manager - being told to work harder after a week of 3am finishes was not what I needed as a young engineer. The stark difference between these two experiences motivated me to become a manager: I wanted every engineer I worked with to have the support I had in the best case.  
  
Since then, as I’ve learned more, I’ve realized that I love the kind of problems I get to solve as a manager. Deeply complex problems with long-term impact both on the company and on people’s lives. One of my proudest achievements is creating a fully transparent pay system, and on the day it was revealed, everybody was happy with it. Nobody stormed out. By spending time thinking deeply about everybody’s pay and ensuring the mechanics of promotion were clear, I put the team in a place where they could see a peer was paid more than them, and it not be a problem.  
  
Despite all this, I love being technical. I sometimes indulge myself and spend a morning writing some code to improve tests or provide better abstractions. If I couldn’t be a manager, I’d be super happy to be an IC.  
  
I’m looking for someone who is passionate. Passionate about both management and being technical. Someone who spots a pattern amongst their team, figures out a better way for us to operate, and then builds the automation that powers it. I introduced a new process that enables engineers to merge 30% of PRs without a human review beforehand. I also built the automation that approves these PRs. I also built that automation with abstractions that make it easy for the engineers to improve the automation themselves.  
  
It can be hard to find seasoned engineering leaders who haven’t succumbed to the status quo in some way or another. We're committed to giving all our people a total and utter lack of terrible managers, and that means we're willing to take a chance on someone early in their leadership journey who's courageous, principled, and has the drive to build themselves into a great leader who can say “Yah I know everyone is doing that, but we won't because...”  
  
Why You  
  
Should or Shouldn’t Apply  
  
Engineering leadership comes in many flavors, not all of which fit our model. I thought I’d outline some things I’m looking for to help you decide if this fits what you’re looking for:  
  
•  
  
You love being technical and can hold in-depth conversations with direct reports from infra to backend to frontend.  
  
•  
  
You enjoy management problems. We want people who get excited about driving people to be their best, giving difficult feedback, and building systems that make this easier  
  
•  
  
You hold your team to a high standard and don’t shy away from getting into the details and giving feedback, even to the best folks on your team.  
  
•  
  
You are an excellent and empathetic communicator. Facilitating change at both an individual and organization level requires understanding how to navigate the beliefs, opinions, and past experiences of engineers and figuring out how to both convince them of a new way of doing things while also leaving yourself open to feedback.  
  
•  
  
You know what exceptional engineers look like. You’ve thought deeply about what makes them tick, how to recruit them, and how to grow folks into them. I want to see depth here, the industry often regurgitates a vanilla description, but the reality is more nuanced.  
  
•  
  
You’re good at thinking about product, business, and maybe even design, but you’re not interested in calling the shots and are more interested in building a team that can make the best decisions without you.  
  
•  
  
You thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments. We're a young startup where leaders wear multiple hats, and you'll build your own (high-speed) on-ramp through developing strong feedback loops.  
  
Put another way, you shouldn’t apply if:  
  
•  
  
You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology.  
  
•  
  
You’ve gotten into management because it was the only growth path available  
  
•  
  
You want to make all the product decisions instead of empowering your team to make those calls.  
  
•  
  
You're happy with a team of engineers that are predominantly early-career, mid-career, or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. With enough guardrails, the team can get things done.  
  
•  
  
A staff or principal engineer to you is someone who spends most of their time project managing or doing architecture reviews.  
  
•  
  
You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently than the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent product delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers.  
  
What We’re Building  
  
Talent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. To accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. Teams struggle to keep up!  
  
Scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. A recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. They must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others.  
  
Ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. In many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here.  
  
We have many customers, great revenue growth, years of runway, and amazing investors like YCombinator, Elad Gil, and Lachy Groom. I’ll share more once we meet.  
  
Engineering Culture  
  
Our engineering culture is motivated by Abhik and Benji’s (our co-founders) belief that a small talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!).  
  
Collaboration is Natural, Communication is Deliberate  
  
Our engineering team (and the team at large) consists of lifelong learners who are humble and kind (meet them here!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally (we filter for it in interviews). We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers can focus 36h out of a 40h work week (Abhik wrote about it here). Even managers can rely on getting consistent time (and support to make, if necessary) to focus and do creative work without the demand of constant meetings.  
  
Increase Leverage, not Team Size  
  
We built Ashby with the quality, breadth, and depth that many customers would expect from much larger teams over larger time scales. We’ve done this through investment in:  
  
•  
  
Great developer tooling. Our CI/CD takes ~10m, and we deploy at least 5x a day. Everyone on the team has contributed to developer experience  
  
•  
  
Building blocks to create powerful and customizable products fast. At the core of Ashby is a set of common components (analytics modeling and query language, policy engine, workflow engine, design system) which we are constantly improving. Each improvement to a common component cascades throughout our app (short video on it here).  
  
•  
  
AI-powered tooling. We think of AI as a way to automate the mundane parts of building and maintaining high-quality software. We use a combination of third-party and internally built tools that, for instance, auto-triage customer issues, suggest fixes, prototype ideas, generate production-ready code, and conduct code reviews. Engineers have an unlimited token budget (but are not measured on it). We write in detail about our philosophy, current use of AI, and future plans for AI in Engineering here.  
  
Here’s an impromptu quote from Arjun in our company Slack of what it’s like to build a feature at Ashby:  
  
And a demo of one of these building blocks:  
  
Give Engineers  
  
Ownership & Autonomy  
  
We, as engineers, find clever ways to solve problems, which amplifies when we deeply understand the problem. All of us in technical leadership did our best work as engineers when we had a deep understanding of the end-user and the business and ownership over the solution. Our engineering culture reflects this experience: engineers own projects end-to-end, from speaking with users to writing product specs to UX design. These are skills that we often don’t get to practice as engineers, and, as a manager at Ashby, you’ll provide mentorship and feedback to engineers to ensure they are successful when delivering projects.  
  
Put Effort into Diversity  
  
Diverse teams drive innovation and better outcomes. As the father of two young girls, I want to see them grow up in a world where all industries are open and welcoming to everyone, regardless of race, gender, or preferences. Helping to build a more diverse team at Ashby is my way of contributing to this change.  
  
Today, 26% of engineers at Ashby are from underrepresented groups. It’s not great, and we are taking conscious steps to improve, like sourcing diverse candidates, providing generous paid family leave, no leetcode interviews, and more.  
  
Interview Process  
  
At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together. Our interview process is six interviews in the following order:  
  
•  
  
Intro Call (30m) - Discuss your application questions, align on the responsibilities of the role, and answer questions about Ashby.  
  
•  
  
Past Experience  
  
Deep Dive (1h) - Discuss your past experience as an engineering leader.  
  
•  
  
Technical  
  
Screen (1h) - Add a feature back to Ashby. You'll spend most of your time understanding a specific part of our codebase and write less than 15 lines of code.  
  
•  
  
Coffee Chat with VP of Engineering (1h) - Spend time with our VP of Engineering and get to know each other.  
  
•  
  
Meet the Team (2h) - At this point, the engineering leadership team is excited about you and you'll meet our CEO, Engineers, Product Managers, and some other folks on the team.  
  
I will be your main point of contact and prepare you for interviews. If we don’t give an offer, we’ll provide feedback!  
  
Technology Stack  
  
I’m sharing our tech stack with the caveat that we don’t require previous experience: TypeScript (frontend & backend), Node.js, React, Apollo GraphQL, Postgres, Redis.  
  
Benefits

Competitive salary and equity.

10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

Unlimited PTO, and we will encourage you to take it.

Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!  
  
•  
  
$100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.  
  
Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

* Assigned workspace in the Toronto and/or London office.

* Supporting corridor and currency expansion by coordinating new banking relationships against the priorities set through the Bank Steering Committee roadmap.

**Account Lifecycle & Global Entity Management**

* Overseeing the complete lifecycle of bank accounts, including onboarding, opening, maintenance, operations, and closure across multiple jurisdictions.

* Maintaining accurate records of the account estate and mandate structures, partnering with Bank Operations to keep network reference data current.

* Conducting bank fee analysis and implementing cost reduction strategies, sharing findings with Bank Operations to inform network governance and prioritization.
* Managing credit facility reporting, budget preparation, and audit support activities.
